newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just easier, market stays slow.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just easier, market stays slow.

text.p: Gold prices managed a mild bounce after the over-the-counter (OTC) options expiry at 1330 GMT but lost height when follow-through buying failed to materialise.

"As far as we can see there was very little going on at the expiry. It's been very quiet," a dealer said. Gold was fixed at $388.50 per ounce after $388.65 this morning and $388.80 previously. New York's Comex December contract was down $0.60 at $393.40 around the gold fixing, after opening lower as forecast.
Options traders said earlier some of the OTC interest was focused on the $390 call which went off well out of the money.
There was little in overnight business to give Europe direction. The New York markets were mainly slightly softer ahead of the expiry and an upcoming three-day weekend.
Tocom gold futures firmed in response to a weaker yen after a below-forecast Bank of Japan business confidence survey.
"The market needs some motivation to trade and it doesn't appear to have much at the moment," a dealer said.
Trade was slowed early in the week first by a holiday in London and Tokyo and then by the OTC option expiry.
The upcoming U.S. Labor Day holiday weekend could slow business for the rest of this week, dealers said.

Dealers said the market overall was receiving some support from physical buying but interest was still low key. "Need some imput to imput to shake up the volatilities which have been so low for so long. But it is difficult to see what could get it started," a dealer said.
The silver price showed some mild volatility after the expiry ranging from $5.18 to $5.24 bid after a morning spent hovering around unchanged at $5.23/$5.25.
The $5.30 call was the most significant strike price.
"It's a flip of a coin whether it goes up or down. I see it going sideways for a while," a dealer said, placing silver in a $5.15-$5.30 range medium term.

Technically it was capable of taking a shot at $5.30 and $5.40 after a couple of good closes and steady firmness through August. But interest remained stubbornly low. "We are still in the summer period and business, especially in the white metals, is particularly quiet," said one analyst.
Platinum ws a little easier at $399.10/$400.10, down $1.50 from the close while palladium was indicated at $125.70/$126.75, up $1.00.
